raw_case_text: A 47-year-old man experienced 2 months of progressive unilateral nasal blockage and recurrent anterior epistaxis. He denied other symptoms such as fever, malaise, weight loss, tinnitus, and diplopia. He was initially diagnosed with a nasal polyp and underwent resection. An initial pathological examination indicated malignancy, and he was referred to our centre. He had a history of 5 repeated falciparum malaria infections within 8 years period during occupational placement in Congo and Papua Island, both of which are malaria-endemic regions. He always received complete treatment for every episode of infection and had not experienced symptoms of malaria for the past 2 years. He lived on Java Island, which is not a malaria-endemic region and where our centre is located. He had no other significant comorbidities, including autoimmune disease and immunodeficiency. Data for previous infection by potential lymphomagenic viruses were not available since examination for these viruses was not available in our region. Upon presentation at our centre, he had a WHO performance status of 0 with an unremarkable physical examination. A repeat biopsy and pathological examination showed CD20 (+), highly proliferative DLBCL (Fig. 1a-c). Contrast CT scan showed a mass on the right maxillary sinus, destroying the posteromedial wall of the maxillary sinus, extending to the nasal cavity, ethmoid sinus, and masticator space, with metastasis to right cervical lymph nodes (Fig. 2a-c). Intracranial spread and distant metastasis were not detected. He was treated with six cycles of R-CHOP every 3 weeks (rituximab 375 mg/m2, cyclophosphamide 750 mg/m2, doxorubicin 50 mg/m2, vincristine 1.4 mg/m2, and prednisone 40 mg/m2 for 5 days) with G-CSF support as needed. He experienced no significant adverse event during chemotherapy. A repeat CT scan was performed 1 month after the completion of chemotherapy, showing a complete response (Fig. 3a-e). One month after CT scan, he experienced shivering, fever, sweating, and a return to normal temperature, which repeated irregularly for roughly 1 week, suggesting malaria. His complete blood count showed haemoglobin of 8 g/dL, haematocrit of 27.6%, leucocyte of 2,000 cells/muL, and platelet count of 10,000 cells/muL. The presence of falciparum malaria was confirmed through immunochromatographic testing of malarial antigen (Plasmotec Malaria-3, Indec Diagnostics, Jakarta, Indonesia). This case was considered a relapse since our centre is not in the malaria-endemic region. He was treated with a fixed drug combination of dihydroartemisinin (40 mg)-piperaquine (320 mg) 4 tablets qd on day 1-3 and primaquine 15 mg qd on day 1 (bodyweight of 61 kg). The patient completed the anti-malarial regimen without any adverse event. He experienced complete symptom resolution, and normalization of complete blood count, with no detected plasmodium on blood smear evaluation.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 47-year-old male presenting with irregular fever, shivering, and sweating of approximately one week's duration.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient presented with a one-week history of cyclical shivering, fever, profuse sweating, and defervescence repeating irregularly roughly one month following completion of chemotherapy. Two months prior to chemotherapy, he had presented with unilateral nasal blockage and epistaxis, leading to resection of a suspected polyp which demonstrated diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL), for which he completed 6 cycles of chemoimmunotherapy with confirmed complete remission.
subjective.past_medical_history: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma of right maxillary sinus (CD20-positive, stage II with cervical lymph node involvement) in complete remission following 6 cycles of R-CHOP (rituximab 375 mg/m2, cyclophosphamide 750 mg/m2, doxorubicin 50 mg/m2, vincristine 1.4 mg/m2, and prednisone 40 mg/m2 for 5 days) completed one month prior. Occupational history: lived on Java Island (non-endemic); prior occupational placement in Congo and Papua Island (malaria-endemic regions) within the past 8 years with 5 treated episodes of malaria, asymptomatic for 2 years prior. No autoimmune disease or known immunodeficiency.
subjective.review_of_systems: Denied malaise, weight loss, tinnitus, diplopia, cough, or dyspnea. Home medications: recent R-CHOP and G-CSF. Allergies: null.

objective.physical_examination: WHO performance status 0. Vital signs and physical examination were unremarkable, without focal lymphadenopathy or hepatosplenomegaly.
objective.routine_investigations: Complete blood count: hemoglobin 8 g/dL, hematocrit 27.6%, leukocytes 2,000 cells/muL, and platelets 10,000 cells/muL. Peripheral blood smear performed.
objective.advanced_workup: Diagnostic tumor biopsy: CD20 (+), highly proliferative DLBCL. Head and neck contrast-enhanced CT (staging and post-treatment): initial CT showed destructive mass of right maxillary sinus extending into nasal cavity, ethmoid sinus, masticator space, and right cervical lymph nodes; post-treatment CT at 1 month showed complete radiographic response.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive diagnosis: Relapse of Plasmodium falciparum malaria secondary to chemotherapy-induced immunosuppression (R-CHOP) in a patient with DLBCL.
Diagnostic confirmation: Positive immunochromatographic malarial antigen test (Plasmotec Malaria-3), with subsequent negative post-treatment blood smear evaluation confirming parasite clearance.
Treatment & Outcome: Treated with fixed-dose oral dihydroartemisinin (40 mg)-piperaquine (320 mg) 4 tablets once daily on days 1-3 and primaquine 15 mg once daily on day 1 (patient weight 61 kg). The patient completed the regimen without adverse events, resulting in complete resolution of fever, normalization of complete blood counts, and eradication of parasitemia.
